column1: # boru Language Specification: the `case` word — dispatch on a value
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `case <value> [m1 b1 m2 b2 … default]` evaluates the value (a
# code-body list executes and its LAST result is captured; parens
# evaluate before collection; a plain value is used as-is), then walks
# the match/block pairs in order. A match that is a code-body list
# executes as if the value were already on the stack ([gt 3] runs
# `v gt 3`) and the result coerces to boolean; any other match
# UNIFIES with the value (equal scalars/atoms, a type literal —
# builtin or def'd — matches its members). The first matching
# clause's block runs the same way — value pushed first, like the
# `error [handler]` block — so a block list can consume it; a plain
# value block is the result as-is. The trailing odd element is the
# optional default. No match and no default produces nothing. The
# stack-value form `<value> case [clauses]` serves contexts where the
# value is already on the stack (e.g. error handlers).
# STATIC EXHAUSTIVENESS (design/case-exhaustiveness.0.md): `boru check`
# requires a case's clauses to cover the scrutinee's static type — a
# default-less case with a provably-uncoverable value is a check ERROR
# (case_not_exhaustive), and `boru run` declines such a program at
# preflight. The default is NOT required when the type disjunctions are
# met: the clauses cover every union alternative / enum member /
# Boolean's true+false / the concrete scrutinee value. Coverage rules:
# a base-type clause does NOT cover a user-minted newtype (a Pos
# scrutinee needs Pos, [is Pos], or Any — not Integer); comparison
# predicates and DepScalar refinements cover numeric domains by
# interval union ([gt 3] plus [lte 3] covers Integer) and [is T]
# covers by the is-relation; a DYNAMIC (untyped or computed) scrutinee
# has no static type to prove coverage, so it REQUIRES a trailing
# default or an Any clause. The historical no-match/no-default
# produce-nothing behaviour is therefore no longer expressible in a
# check-clean program (the engine still produces nothing when an
# unchecked run falls through). §6 pins the check-clean shapes.
# §1  value matches (unify)
case 2 [1 "one" 2 "two" "many"]
column3: an equal scalar matches

column1: case 9 [1 "one" 2 "two" "many"]
column3: no match takes the default

column1: def f fn [[x:Any][String][case x [1 "one" "other"]]] f 9
column3: a dynamic scrutinee REQUIRES the default (or an Any clause) — the checker cannot prove coverage of an unknown type

column1: case red/q [red/q "warm" blue/q "cool"]
column3: atoms match by equality

column1: case 2.0 [2 "int-two" "other"]
column3: unify is exact across numeric leaves — 2.0 does not match 2

column1: # §2  type matches
case "x" [Integer "int" String "str" "other"]
column3: a builtin type literal matches its members

column1: case 5 [Integer "int" String "str" "other"]
column3: …tried in order

column1: case true [Integer "int" "other"]
column3: non-members fall through

column1: def Pos refine Integer def x:Pos 5 case x [Pos "pos" Integer "plain-int" "other"]
column3: a def'd newtype matches nominally

column1: def Pos refine Integer case 5 [Pos "pos" Integer "plain-int" "other"]
column3: …matches follow UNIFY (construction compatibility): a newtype admits its base values here

column1: def Pos refine Integer case 5 [[is Pos] "pos" "other"]
column3: …use an [is T] predicate match for nominal strictness

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) case 50 [Big "big" Integer "small-int"]
column3: a predicate refinement runs its predicate

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) case 5 [Big "big" Integer "small-int"]
column3: …and rejects values outside it

column1: # §3  predicate matches (code-body lists run with the value on the stack)
case 5 [[gt 3] "big" "small"]
column3: [gt 3] executes as `5 gt 3`

column1: case 2 [[gt 3] "big" "small"]
column3: a false predicate falls through

column1: case 5 [[gt 3] [mul 10] "small"]
column3: a block list also sees the value — here consuming it

column1: case 7 [[lt 3] "low" [lt 10] "mid" "high"]
column3: predicates are tried in order

column1: # §4  the value expression executes
case (1 add 1) [2 "two" "other"]
column3: a paren group evaluates before dispatch

column1: case [1 add 1] [2 "two" "other"]
column3: a code-body value executes; the LAST result is captured

column1: def f fn [[x:Integer] [] []] case [f 1] [2 "two" "other"]
column3: a value expression that produces nothing is loud

column1: case 1 Integer
column3: the clause list must be a list

column1: # §5  stack-value form — the value is already on the stack
5 case [5 "five" "other"]
column3: `v case [clauses]` reads the value from the stack

column1: def e (do [raise bad_input "nope"]) do [e dot code case [bad_input/q "B" "other"]]
column3: …the natural shape inside error handlers

column1: # §6  static exhaustiveness — default-less cases whose clauses cover the
# scrutinee's static type run clean (these rows double as check-accuracy
# canaries: the checker must NEVER flag them)
def IS (Integer tor String) def f fn [[x:IS][String][case x [Integer "i" String "s"]]] f 5
column3: a declared union covered by its type clauses needs no default

column1: def IS (Integer tor String) def f fn [[x:IS][String][case x [Integer "i" String "s"]]] f "x"
column3: …every alternative dispatches

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean][Integer][case b [true 1 false 0]]] f false
column3: true+false cover Boolean

column1: def Color (red/q tor green/q tor blue/q) def f fn [[c:Color][String][case c [red/q "r" green/q "g" blue/q "b"]]] f green/q
column3: every enum member listed needs no default

column1: def MaybeInt (Integer tor none) def f fn [[x:MaybeInt][Integer][case x [Integer 1 none 0]]] f 5
column3: a none-able optional covered by Integer+none

column1: def IS (Integer tor String) def f fn [[x:IS][Integer][case x [[gt 3] 0 Integer 1 String 2]]] f 2
column3: predicates compose with type clauses over a union

column1: def f fn [[x:Integer][Integer][case x [[gt 3] 1 [lte 3] 2]]] f 5
column3: comparison predicates prove coverage by interval union — [gt 3] plus [lte 3] covers Integer

column1: def Big (Integer gt 10) def f fn [[x:Integer][String][case x [Big "big" [lte 10] "small"]]] f 5
column3: a DepScalar refinement match contributes its bounds; its complement completes the domain

column1: def Pos refine Integer def Neg refine Integer def PN (Pos tor Neg) def f fn [[x:PN][String][case x [Pos "p" Neg "n"]]] def y:Pos 5 f y
column3: newtype alternatives are covered by their own clauses — Integer would cover NEITHER (nominal boundary)

column1: def Pos refine Integer def Neg refine Integer def PN (Pos tor Neg) def f fn [[x:PN][String][case x [[is Pos] "pos" [is Neg] "neg"]]] def y:Neg 7 f y
column3: …[is T] predicates cover nominally too

column1: case 2 [1 "one" 2 "two"]
column3: a concrete scrutinee that provably matches a clause needs no default

column1: # §7  the open-call default arm (NUR048 fix, was SHARP-EDGES G9). A
#     match-position word bound to a FUNCTION VALUE can never be a
#     genuine match (a function unifies with nothing), so it heads an
#     OPEN-CALL default: the rest of the list is one default arm, run
#     exactly like a matched code-body arm — isolated, value pushed
#     first — instead of being torn into bogus (match, block) pairs
#     whose last token leaked out as the silent "result".
def g fn [[s:Map e:Map] [Map] [s]] def st {a:1} def ev {k:9} case "z" ["q" [drop "quit"] g st ev nip]
column3: an open-call default collects its own written args (was: silently returned ev); the arm consumes the pushed value like any block

column1: def g fn [[s:Map e:Map] [Map] [s]] def st {a:1} def ev {k:9} case "q" ["q" [drop "quit"] g st ev nip]
column3: a matching pair still wins; the open-call default is not taken

column1: def g fn [[s:Map e:Map] [Map] [s]] def st {a:1} def ev {k:9} case "z" ["q" ["quit"] (g st ev)]
column3: the paren spelling keeps its meaning: a single-element default block

column1: def h fn [[s:String] [String] [s add "!"]] case "z" ["q" ["quit"] h]
column3: a single trailing fn word dispatches against the case value in isolation

column1: def red "R" case "R" [red "matched" "other"]
column3: a bare word bound to a NON-fn value keeps its match reading (resolves to the def'd value)

column1: case zed/q [zed "matched" "other"]
column3: …and an unbound bare word keeps its atom-match reading
